mediaPolicy.hero: Use attributed, location-specific hero photography. Never substitute another locality's landmark.
mediaPolicy.recommendations: Provider imagery is the first choice in both the day-plan strip and recommendation gallery; use a locality-safe curated asset or deterministic authored artwork only when provider media is unavailable.
mediaPolicy.iasiFallback: Use the clearly labeled generated Iași panorama and recommendation assets for the offline seed experience; never imply that they are documentary photography.

narrative.overview: WeatherWise is a bright European travel atlas, not a dark weather dashboard. A quiet paper navigation row opens into an asymmetric daylight field: editorial temperature, precise weather narrative, a broad cartographic arc, a condition-aware sky, and one white planning strip. The sequence is deliberate—search a place, read its daylight story, scan chromatic forecast tabs, then open one practical plan. Warm ivory paper and atlas-blue ink establish calm authority. Azure rules, golden daylight, coral and mint accents add optimism without turning the interface into a generic dashboard grid. Display weather and section titles use bookish Georgia with the platform serif fallback; controls, dense facts, and explanatory copy use the platform system sans. Material 3 and native navigation behavior remain the interaction foundation. The approved direction is `.impeccable/mocks/decision/atlas-de-lumina.png`, selected on 2026-10-06 from built-in ImageGen exploration and recorded by its adjacent prompt and JSON sidecar. Direction seed `97c9e211` is the reproducibility key. The implemented visual truth is `frontend/lib/theme/atlas_theme.dart` plus the home and trip-planner surfaces; `.impeccable/review/desktop.png` (1280×720), `.impeccable/review/mobile.png` (390×844), and the `trip-planner-result-{desktop,mobile}.png` captures are the shipped review evidence. Disposition: **SHIP**. Preserve this system rather than merging it with the retired Forecast Focus identity.
keyCharacteristics: Bright paper navigation and an authored, condition-aware daylight field.
Editorial serif temperature and headings paired with highly legible system sans UI.
One white plan strip as the bridge between forecast facts and recommendations.
Chromatic forecast tabs that behave like an atlas index, not a stack of cards.
Fine map-like rules, tabular numerals, restrained depth, and generous whitespace.
Location-symbolic hero photography and real recommendation media, with attributed provider imagery and clearly labeled illustrative seed assets.
Finite fade-and-slide state changes that become instant when reduced motion is requested.
Complete English/Romanian copy may wrap without changing hierarchy or discarding state.
A responsive trip-planner form resolves into a quiet, provider-attributed day timeline without inventing certainty, availability, or quality.
Account access and the personal trip library extend the same daylight-and-paper system with explicit restoring, busy, empty, error, and destructive states.

rules.name: The Daylight Owns the Canvas Rule
rules.body: Ivory and paper remain dominant; weather color changes the atmosphere and tab accent, not the entire planning stream.

rules.name: The One Golden Action Rule
rules.body: Gold identifies the primary next step for the selected day. Do not spend it on generic decoration or several equal actions.

rules.name: The Semantic Weather Rule
rules.body: Forecast states always pair color with icon, label, border, or selection semantics; color alone never carries meaning.

rules.name: The Editorial-Utility Split Rule
rules.body: Georgia is for the weather story and object titles; system sans is for interaction, dense facts, and operational copy.

rules.name: The Forecast First Rule
rules.body: Temperature owns display scale. Preserve its visual priority even when Romanian copy or large text increases surrounding height.

rules.name: The Action Labels Stay Sans Rule
rules.body: Every actionable label—including trip creation, retry, date picking, dropdowns, and linked itinerary rows—uses the platform system sans at a decisive weight. Never inherit Georgia merely because the action sits beside an editorial heading.

rules.name: The Same Story, New Measure Rule
rules.body: Responsive adaptation changes stacking and column count, never the information order or the plan-strip handoff.

rules.name: The Reachable Overlay Rule
rules.body: Predictive place results stay anchored over the daylight field without reflowing it; long sheets scroll their variable content while completion actions remain reachable.

rules.name: The Chronology Survives Compression Rule
rules.body: The trip timeline keeps one top-to-bottom time rail on compact and wide layouts; responsive changes may wrap metadata, but never reorder the day's slots or hide an unfilled period.

rules.name: The Paper Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: Use separation, line, and tonal contrast first; shadow is reserved for the plan handoff and transient overlays.

rules.name: The No Glass Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are opaque or near-opaque paper. Do not introduce blur-heavy glassmorphism.

rules.name: The One Broad Curve Rule
rules.body: The daylight field's 24dp lower edge is the signature large curve; downstream content stays within the disciplined 10–16dp family.

rules.name: The Preferences Stay in Context Rule
rules.body: Personalization belongs inside the existing trip form, after the core controls and before the one gold action. Use wrapped native chips and conditional provider-honesty copy; never promote optional preferences into a competing card, wizard step, or promise of verified dietary safety.

rules.name: The Schedule Tells the Truth Rule
rules.body: Pace defines the day's actual operating window and activity count. Display contract-provided start/end times, known duration, and routing state consistently from generated result through saved trip. A live route may name duration and distance; a rhythm fallback must say that it is only reserved time. Never invent precision or compress away the free evening promised by Relaxed pace.

rules.name: The Route Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Show route metadata only for coordinate-backed stops. Distinguish provider-calculated duration and distance from an explicitly approximate, mode-named buffer; omit an unknown leg instead of guessing it, and close every routed day with one return leg from its final located stop.

rules.name: The State Before Transition Rule
rules.body: Account and personal-library surfaces always show whether the session or collection is restoring, busy, empty, failed, or ready before offering the next action; never leave stale content looking current during an unresolved request.

rules.name: The Complete Replacement Rule
rules.body: A saved itinerary remains the trusted visible plan until weather replanning returns a complete replacement. Never clear or partially mutate it during the request; success swaps the whole plan, while failure preserves the prior version and offers a retry.

rules.name: The One-Stop Swap Rule
rules.body: Replacing one saved stop preserves its time, position, and every other stop. Keep the current stop visible until a complete alternative returns; during the request, name the work, show a spinner, and lock competing mutations. After success, restore baseline rhythm times and recalculate route metadata, schedule fit, and the final return leg for the whole day. No-alternative and provider-failure outcomes use distinct copy, preserve the stop, and offer Retry.

dos: Do preserve the daylight-story → plan-strip → forecast-tabs → chart → ideas sequence at every width.
Do use Georgia for editorial display moments and the system sans for UI and dense facts.
Do keep ivory and paper dominant, with gold reserved for the primary day-planning action.
Do keep every available fact in a responsive wrap and use tabular numerals for weather data.
Do keep search suggestions anchored, reject stale responses, and preserve the full picker for deliberate ambiguity handling.
Do localize WeatherWise-owned copy in English and Romanian without resetting the active location, selected day, expanded context, filters, plans, profiles, or reminders.
Do retain provider attribution and clearly distinguish live, demo, cached, and unverified availability states.

Do clear a rendered trip plan as soon as any plan-defining input or preference changes, then show results only for the submitted dates, pace, transport, radius, interests, dietary intent, and meal budget.
Do keep trip preferences inline, optional, and wrapped at compact widths; use paper for unselected chips, sky for selected chips, and conditional provider-honesty copy for dietary intent.
Do explain pace before generation, then preserve its day span, activity count, travel buffer, start/end times, and known durations in both generated and saved plans.
Do distinguish calculated routes from approximate mode-named buffers, surface schedule adjustments and unresolved conflicts, and preserve the final return leg after a stop replacement.
Do keep the trip timeline chronological and legible at compact widths, with rating, review count, source, and distance allowed to wrap.
Do keep account status and personal-trip loading, empty, error, retry, and deletion outcomes explicit, localized, and compatible with native autofill and navigation.
Do honor reduced motion, safe areas, large text, keyboard reachability, and 48dp Android / 44pt iOS targets.
donts: Don't revive the dark Forecast Focus palette, teal atmospheric slab, or sans-only identity.
Don't turn the page into a generic dashboard grid or elevate every object into a card.
Don't show a landmark from another place, imply that illustrative imagery is documentary, or ship an unattributed raster.
Don't use the approved comp itself as live geographic evidence; it is directional artwork.
Don't introduce glassmorphism, gradient text, looping atmosphere motion, or decorative shadows.
Don't use color alone for weather, selection, availability, warning, or error meaning.
Don't make loading or fallback plan signals look tappable, or let a stale plan survive a place/day change.
Don't imply that an account is required for the core forecast flow, expose a private trip before authentication resolves, or delete a trip without confirmation that names it.
Don't present a provider rating as a WeatherWise score, show a star without its review count, invent a dining rating, or imply that a 50 km radius is the itinerary's total distance.
Don't place optional trip preferences in nested cards or a separate wizard step, and don't imply that a dietary search match is a verified menu or allergen-safety guarantee.
Don't invent an exact activity duration, hide a contract-provided end time, or schedule a third activity into the Relaxed pace's free evening.
Don't guess a route for a coordinate-less stop, present reserved buffer time as provider-calculated travel, or omit an early-departure or walking/bicycle caution when the route requires it.
Don't translate provider-authored names, descriptions, availability data, URLs, images, or attribution.
